The twin radio galaxy J104455+354055 provides a unique possibility to study the interplay of radio jets of two radio galaxies. The analysis of the properties of the magnetic fields observed along the radio jets suggests that the wiggles and bends of these jets, caused by the likely interactions of the host galaxies, could be also governed by the magnetic fields that may prevent them from merging. The derived strengths and energies of the magnetic field in different parts of the jets should allow us to improve the magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations of radio galaxies.

title: The system initial mass function of Orion OB1b from probabilistic Gaia DR3 memberships
summary: [ABRIDGED] Context: Whether the initial mass function (IMF) varies with environment remains a central question in star formation. The multiple populations of Orion OB1b provide an ideal laboratory to test possible IMF variations. Aims: We aim to characterise the stellar populations of Orion OB1b by identifying its constituent groups, assigning membership probabilities to individual sources, and determining their IMFs. Methods: Using Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry, we identified stellar groups through clustering analysis and assigned membership probabilities with a probabilistic mixture model. Stellar masses were derived from extinction-corrected photometry using pre-main-sequence evolutionary models. Results: We identified eight kinematically distinct groups and a non-clustered population, deriving ages and IMFs spanning ${\sim}0.08$--$10\,M_\odot$ for six groups, all consistent with being gravitationally unbound. Each IMF was fitted with a lognormal distribution below $1M_\odot$ and a power law above. The high-mass regime is statistically indistinguishable across all groups, while four groups also exhibit consistent IMFs over the full mass range. The remaining two groups show differences that may reflect membership uncertainties rather than intrinsic IMF variations. The combined IMF is characterised by $m_c=0.27^{+0.02}_{-0.02},M_\odot$, $σ=0.45^{+0.03}_{-0.03}$, and $Γ=1.85^{+0.16}_{-0.14}$. The non-clustered population exhibits a broader and more uncertain IMF, although residual field contamination cannot be ruled out. Conclusions: Our results support previous evidence for the complex internal structure of OB1b. The IMF in OB1b appears broadly consistent across its kinematically distinct groups and compatible with other young populations in Orion.

title: Unresolved binaries from Gaia XP to SPHEREx
summary: Unresolved companions alter the luminosity and spectra of a star, but a colour-magnitude diagram (CMD) reveals them only when the system is over-luminous, and a Gaia photocentre orbit constrains only a combination of the mass and flux ratios. We fit the absolute Gaia BP/RP (XP) and SPHEREx spectra (XPS) of about 71,000 low-mass stars in the Gaia Catalogue of Nearby Stars with the J-CaPS XPS emulator, which predicts single-star and coeval-binary spectra on an absolute flux scale. First, more than half of known binaries lie within the main-sequence (MS) band of the CMD, because the companion is faint or lifts a metal-poor primary onto the single-star ridge. XPS recovers 86 per cent of the binaries that a CMD cut finds and 44 per cent of those it misses. Second, a small photocentre motion can come from a faint companion or a luminous one of nearly equal mass. XPS distinguishes them and recovers the mass ratios of double-lined binaries. Among substellar candidates with radial-velocity follow-up, it ranks all 11 binaries above all 16 confirmed brown-dwarf or planet hosts. The public package spbin provides this check before follow-up. Third, where XPS detects no companion light, we place an upper limit on the light of an MS companion. Among Gaia DR3 astrometric orbits with clean spectral fits, 2841 require more companion mass than XPS allows for a single MS star. Within 200 pc, their companion masses cluster at those of typical white dwarfs, and nearly circular orbits support this interpretation. Of 24 companions that joint radial-velocity and astrometric orbits show to be faint, XPS recovers 22, compared with 14 selected by the absence of a colour excess. Applied to forthcoming Gaia DR4 orbital solutions, XPS can help distinguish luminous binaries from substellar companions and identify candidate compact companions whose dynamical masses exceed the limits allowed by their light.

title: Using fixed $w$ to reproduce evolving $w_0$-$w_a$ dark energy at the field level
summary: Recent results from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) hint at dynamical dark energy, making the accurate modelling of such cosmologies increasingly important for future analyses. In this work, we show that because, when written in superconformal time $τ$, the $N$-body equations of motion depend on the background cosmology only through the expansion history $a(τ)$, matching $a(τ)$ allows us to map one cosmology onto another. As a first, observationally relevant, application of this new method, we match a Chevallier--Polarski--Linder (CPL) cosmology to a constant-$w$ cosmology with the closest $a(τ)$. This allows us to use a single fixed-$w$ simulation to reproduce the simulation predictions of the target CPL cosmology at the field level at redshifts $0\le z\le3$. We validate this matching with 100 pairs of CPL and fixed-$w$ \textsc{mg-glam} simulations, spanning $0.1\leΩ_{\rm m}\le0.5$, $-1.4\le w_0\le-0.5$ and $-1.8\le w_a\le-0.15$. For a DESI-like cosmology, the matter power spectra of the matched and target simulations agree to 0.24\% for $k\lesssim1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ and 0.8\% up to $k\lesssim3\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ at $0\le z\le3$, and the density phases are reproduced with a stochasticity below 0.02\%. Displacements, velocities, momenta, redshift-space multipoles, bispectra and the halo and void abundances are similarly well predicted. For most models we consider, we achieve subpercent error in the power spectrum up to scales $k\lesssim1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ at all redshifts, with density stochasticity below 0.03\% over the same scales. The method allows constant-$w$ simulations and field-level emulators to be used for CPL cosmologies, and generalises to any cosmology with no additional scale dependence.

title: Finite-Temperature Stabilization of a KKLT Modulus in Three-Dimensional Lattice Simulations
summary: We investigate the cosmological stabilization of a KKLT modulus through three-dimensional Langevin lattice simulations incorporating an evolving thermal bath, dissipation, spatial gradients, and stochastic fluctuations. While the spatially averaged modulus closely follows homogeneous evolution away from the capture threshold, near-critical trajectories linger near the unstable potential barrier for approximately one e-fold, allowing long-wavelength fluctuations to undergo tachyonic amplification and drive localized regions across the barrier even as the mean field turns back toward the stabilized vacuum. Linear Langevin theory reproduces the fluctuation growth, while convergence tests identify a narrow stochastic layer in which the barrier-crossing fraction shows no systematic dependence on the discretization at a fixed effective distance from the threshold. These results demonstrate that capture of the spatially averaged modulus does not guarantee that every spatial region remains within the stabilizing barrier.

title: Environmental dependence of the properties of H$α$ emitters in the extremely massive galaxy protoclusters BOSS1244 and BOSS1542 at $z = 2.24$
summary: Protoclusters, the progenitors of galaxy clusters, provide ideal laboratories for studying how high-density environments influence galaxy formation and evolution at early cosmic epochs. It remains unclear whether environmental effects on galaxy properties over scales of $>30$ cMpc are already in place at $z > 2$ and how these effects depend on the evolutionary stage of large-scale structures. We investigate the physical properties of H$α$ emitters (HAEs) in two extremely overdense protoclusters, BOSS1244 and BOSS1542, at $z = 2.24$, and explore the environmental dependence of galaxy properties at this redshift. In BOSS1244, we find a clear color-density and stellar mass-density relation. HAEs in higher-density regions are significantly redder in $z_{\rm s}-K_{\rm s}$ and more massive than those in lower-density regions. In contrast, BOSS1542 shows weak or no such correlations. Red HAEs $(z_{\rm s}-K_{\rm s}>2.5)$ in both fields are preferentially located in the densest cores, have high stellar masses $(>10^{11}\,M_{\odot})$, high SFRs, and are $4-7$ times more abundant than in general fields. The irregular morphologies observed in some red HAEs are consistent with ongoing mass assembly and may be associated with dust-obscured star formation or galaxy interactions. Both protoclusters broadly follow the star-forming main sequence, but BOSS1542 exhibits a steeper slope, indicating more active star formation in massive galaxies. Our results demonstrate that environmental effects on galaxy properties operate over scales of $\sim39$\,cMpc at $z=2.24$, but their manifestation is strongly dependent on the evolutionary state of the large-scale structure. BOSS1244 appears more evolved, with ongoing galaxy merging and possible quenching, while BOSS1542 remains in an early, filamentary, gas-rich phase.

title: DIPS-OjOS I: Project Design and Science Validation
summary:
Automated pipelines and machine-learning algorithms are efficient at detecting standard planetary transits, but can miss subtle, non-periodic morphological anomalies. We present the pilot phase of DIPS-OjOS (Detecting Irregular Photometric Signals - OjímetrO Survey), a professional-amateur collaboration designed to develop and validate a scalable workflow for identifying irregular photometric signals in exoplanet transit light curves through trained visual inspection. The project targets starspot-crossing events, stellar flares, circumplanetary structures, exomoon-like signatures, and transit-duration or timing anomalies overlooked by automated searches.
  We built the infrastructure required for a controlled visual-inspection experiment: simulated control light curves, preparation and detrending of real short-cadence Kepler data, a transit-modeling pipeline that computes an optimized average transit profile for each light curve, and a web-based classification platform. The real sample was deliberately restricted to 51 well-characterized Kepler systems. Collaborators inspected 917 transit events: 555 real transits and 362 simulated controls. The simulated sample quantified observer performance and calibrated a weighted consensus scheme; collaborators recovered injected signals with an average efficiency of 87.6%, while the null-case false-positive rate was 15.3%.
  After expert validation, we retained 88 viable candidate anomalies from the real sample, including 26 starspot-crossing event candidates across eight targets, seven stellar flares, 31 systematic transit-duration deviations motivating refined orbital parameters in four systems, and a mutual transit event in Kepler-89. Recovering candidate signals in this well-studied sample validates the sensitivity of DIPS-OjOS and establishes the basis for future applications to Kepler, TESS, PLATO, and ground-based datasets.

title: Exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon field in planar systems with an arbitrary number of uniform layers
summary: Scalar fields have long been investigated as a potential dark energy candidate. Of these models, screened scalar fields like the chameleon have received interest due to their ability to avoid observational constraints. However, the non-linear nature of these models has led to there being only a small number of exact analytic solutions within the literature. In this work, we present exact analytic solutions for the $n=1$ chameleon model in a planar system consisting of $N$ discrete regions of uniform density. We compare these to the relevant approximate solutions within the literature. We also use our solutions to forecast constraints from CANNEX, a recent experiment devised to measure Casimir forces and detect hypothetical fifth forces. Unlike in previous works, we consider the full fifteen-layered setup of CANNEX, as opposed to treating the plate and wall as single uniform objects. Doing so revealed an increase in the induced chameleon pressure of up to $\sim 7 \%$. However, the resulting gain is insufficient to probe new regions of parameter space at the projected sensitivities.

title: Lithium rich stars in M67: Searching for hot companions through UV observations
summary: Lithium-rich (Li-rich) stars are a rare class of objects characterized by an abnormally high Li abundance in their atmospheres. Although several explanations, including binary interactions, have been proposed, their origin remains uncertain. We aim to search for hot companions to the known Li-rich stars in M67, characterize these stars, and evaluate the binary hypothesis as a possible explanation for their Li enhancement. We combined archival ultraviolet photometry from UVIT/AstroSat, GALEX, and Swift/UVOT with optical and infrared photometry to create multiwavelength spectral energy distributions (SEDs) and search for hot companions. We also used high-resolution archival UVES spectra to look for chemical signatures of past binary interactions. Two known Li-rich stars in M67, WOCS6008 and WOCS2003, show a significant far-UV excess relative to a single-star SED fit, attributed to a companion in the former and to stellar activity in the latter. We thus report the first detection of a hot companion to the Li-rich star, WOCS6008, in M67, offering direct evidence of the role of binary interactions in its Li enrichment. The companion is found to be an extremely low-mass (ELM) white dwarf (WD) of $\sim 0.16\pm0.01 M_{\odot}$, consistent with its kinematic mass, and an age of 2.5 Gyr. We find no enhancement of Na or s-process elements and no depletion of C or Mg in WOCS6008, suggesting that mass transfer during the asymptotic giant branch or red giant branch stage is unlikely. Its derived abundances support a scenario in which this star is the accretor in a binary system that underwent early Case B mass transfer. Our results support previous suggestions that stellar rotation is the most favored mechanism for the Li enrichment in this post-interaction system. Overall, the available evidence supports the case for binary interactions as one of the channels to form Li-rich stars.

title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). Learning machine learning: Investigating the complementarity and biases of strong gravitational lens finding networks on Euclid data
summary: The Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1) strong lens search presents ECLIPSE, the largest catalogue of strong gravitational lens candidates to date, with >15 000 systems identified across 1900 deg2 of sky. It was constructed using five neural networks applied to approximately 68 million galaxies, followed by citizen science and expert visual inspection. In this work, we compare how the independently developed networks use image information to identify their selection of strong lens candidates. The search combines convolutional neural networks and a vision transformer, using the same pool of data but with different image processing and training choices. We investigate why these networks find different systems and what that means for the completeness of our catalogue. We evaluate all networks on a 50 deg2 calibration set and their application to the full DR1 sample. We find that the networks score candidates very differently, and that combining them recovers over 500 lens candidates within our calibration set at an inspection budget of 2000 objects. On the full DR1 sample, we show that individual networks have distinct biases: some networks favour systems with a larger Einstein radius while others are more sensitive to compact configurations. We also investigate network preferences in terms of lens light profile, mass distribution geometry, photometric redshift, and magnitudes. These findings provide a detailed analysis of how neural network selection biases have shaped the Euclid DR1 ECLIPSE catalogue. The results inform how networks should be combined in future Euclid data releases and upcoming wide-field surveys such as LSST or Roman to maximise both completeness and diversity of the recovered lens population.

title: JAISP: A Joint Rubin-Euclid Foundation Model for Cross-Instrument Source Detection and Astrometry
summary: Joint pixel-level processing of Rubin and Euclid imaging promises deeper source detection and the cross-survey consistency that precision cosmology requires. We introduce JAISP (Joint AI Survey Processing), a foundation model that learns a single representation of ten-band imaging: Rubin ugrizy and Euclid VIS, Y, J, and H, from the first public releases over $\approx 0.2$ deg$^2$ of the ECDFS deep field. Trained without labels by predicting each band from the other nine, its frozen encoder drives small task-specific networks for source detection and astrometry. The detection network recovers nearly all VIS-selected Euclid Q1 catalog sources on held-out sky, and source injection shows that combining all ten bands extends the point-source detection limit by $\approx 0.3$ mag beyond VIS alone. The astrometry network transfers the sharp VIS localization to the other nine bands, reducing median cross-band positional offsets from $\approx 50$ to $6$--$10$ mas while retaining the full precision of its VIS centroid anchor even for faint sources. Separating this per-source scatter exposes the cross-survey concordance field: a coherent $9$--$10$ mas offset between the two independently Gaia-registered astrometric solutions, dominated by a component common to all bands. Applied without retraining to a second Euclid Deep Field, both networks perform without measurable loss. These gains serve the joint-survey science case: a deeper census recovers faint neighbors whose blending biases weak-lensing shapes and photometric redshifts, and VIS-grade positions in every band supply the common astrometric reference that joint photometry and faint-source proper motions require. A single representation learned once from survey pixels thus serves several measurements across the sky.

title: Preliminary evidence for a Universal Magnetic Field Configuration in Disk-Galaxy Halos with POSSUM
summary: We use the POSSUM catalog with its high density of background RM sources (30-50 per square degree) to extend previous LOFAR work and investigate the sign of galactic halo magnetic fields. We are searching for the universal configuration that arises if halo magnetization originates from a central Cosmic Battery, and is subsequently transported outward by large-scale outflows. Our analysis considers 10 edge-on galaxies in the field of view of the POSSUM survey with angular sizes between 60 and 100. For each such galaxy we collect all available background RM sources in a circular region with a radius of 2? around it. We rescale all galaxy sizes and their associated background RM source distances to a common galaxy size of 100 and stack all these regions together. We divide the stacked configuration of RM sources into the four quadrants on either side of the stacked galaxy axis. The mean RM of background sources is computed in each quadrant, and we obtain a pattern of positive and negative mean RM values around the stacked galaxy. A consistent, systematic RM-gradient pattern emerges inside about 6 stacked galactic radii, as expected in Magnetic Disk-Winds with the axial magnetic field configuration predicted by the Cosmic Battery. The inferred large-scale axial electric current in the halo flows from the center outwards. Beyond 6 galactic radii we observe the reverse mean RM pattern, as expected in the axial Magnetic Black-Hole Jet configuration predicted by the Cosmic Battery. Our work confirms the prediction of the Cosmic Battery, and presents one of the very few known signatures of the magnetic field in the halo and the circumgalactic medium (CGM).

title: Constraining Planet Nine with Pulsar Timing: Orbit Determination Method from the Acceleration, Jerk, and Snap of the Solar System Barycenter
summary: Planet Nine is hypothesized to exist in the outer solar system in order to explain the physical orbital clustering of several trans-Neptunian objects. A Planet Nine would systematically change the location of the solar system barycenter (SSB). Therefore, the precise timing properties of millisecond radio pulsars would measure the acceleration, jerk, and snap of the currently-perceived SSB under the gravitational influence of a Planet Nine. We present a method on how to use pulsar spin frequency derivatives and binary pulsar orbital period derivatives to constrain the Planet Nine parameter space. We find that searches for unidentified massive objects in the solar system require at least cubic and quartic variations in the pulse times of arrival (corresponding to jerk and snap, respectively) in order to uniquely constrain an orbit. Otherwise, additional assumptions are required to fully constrain the mass and orbital parameters of the object. We use our method to weigh the ice giants Uranus and Neptune and obtain results consistent with the literature. This method could be used to weigh a Planet Nine after a putative optical detection. Future work will use updated pulsar timing datasets that benefit from longer observational baselines and advances in statistical modeling and noise characterization.

title: ACT Excited: Reconciling Starobinsky and Quadratic Chaotic Inflationary Models with ACT Results via Excited States
summary: Data Release 6 of the Atacama Cosmology Telescope, combined with Planck, CMB lensing and DESI BAO data, favours a higher scalar spectral index $n_{s}$ than Planck and a mildly positive running $α_{s}$, putting the Starobinsky model in tension with the data, while the quadratic chaotic model is already excluded by its large tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. We show that relaxing the Bunch--Davies assumption for the initial state of the scalar perturbations can restore agreement without modifying the inflaton potential. Parametrising the Bogoliubov coefficients by an excitation parameter $χ_{S}$ and a relative phase $2\varphi_{S}$, we derive the shifts of $n_{s}$ and $α_{s}$ induced by their scale dependence and map the regions of the $(\varphi_{S},χ_{S})$ plane compatible with the $1σ$ ACT DR6 ranges, the bound $r<0.038$, and the requirement that the scale of new physics $Λ$ exceed the Hubble scale $H$. For the Starobinsky model, a scale-dependent $χ_{S}$ or $\varphi_{S}$ works almost everywhere in this plane: only small neighbourhoods of $\varphi_{S}=0,π$ with $χ_{S}\gtrsim1.22$ are excluded, and a scale-dependent phase fails at $\varphi_{S}=0,π/2,π$ and at $χ_{S}=0$, where the required ${\rm d}\varphi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k$ and ${\rm d}^2\varphi_{S}/{\rm d}(\ln k)^2$ diverge. For the QC model, the excited state must also suppress $r$, which requires $χ_{S}\gtrsim0.63$ and $Λ\lesssim6H$. A scale-dependent $χ_{S}$ must satisfy $|{\rm d}χ_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k|\gtrsim0.0021$ in both models, and in the QC model we show analytically that $0.0021\lesssim{\rm d}χ_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k\lesssim0.0058$ and $0.0008\lesssim{\rm d}^2χ_{S}/{\rm d}(\ln k)^2\lesssim0.0062$. If the tensor modes remain in the BD state, the scenario also predicts a violation of the consistency relation $r=-8n_{T}$, testable once the tensor power spectrum and its tilt are measured.

title: Analysis of the Cosmos 2612 - ICEYE-X36 rendezvous and proximity operation from public orbital element data
summary: We analyse the October 2026 close approach between Cosmos 2612 (NORAD 68762) and the commercial radar satellite ICEYE-X36 (NORAD 59103), both in sun-synchronous low Earth orbit, to determine whether it was a rendezvous and proximity operation (RPO) or the result of natural orbital evolution. The public general perturbations (GP) element history from April to October 2026 was propagated with SGP4, and the prediction error was measured empirically for each object. The null hypothesis of natural evolution, tested with manoeuvre-free propagations, is rejected for all 18 parameter combinations: the encounter required manoeuvres by Cosmos 2612, whereas those of ICEYE-X36 are not needed to reproduce it. Closest approach occurred on 18 October at 06:33 UTC, below 0.79 km (95th percentile), with a local relative velocity of about 0.08 m/s and 41.4 h continuously within 5 km. It was the final stage of a sequence that began in May with a plane match, followed by a phasing drift, the approach and a manoeuvred retreat, with a minimum cumulative $Δv$ of 174-180 m/s. The data cannot resolve the minimum distance below their accuracy, nor establish whether the operation was cooperative or its purpose.

title: On the subtleties of statistical isotropy in cosmic topology
summary: The cosmological principle assumes homogeneity and isotropy on the largest scales for which the cosmic microwave background (CMB) provides the best testing grounds. Here, an analysis of the statistical isotropy for the CMB in the case of the cubic 3-torus topology is presented. Since the statistical anisotropy in the CMB 3-torus sky maps is very tiny, the analysis requires very large ensembles consisting of 100000 CMB simulations in order to reveal deviations from the isotropy. Orbit sum rules, which also have applications in quantum chaos, are used to describe the anisotropy structures found in the torus ensembles. They relate the length of orbits, which connect a given point on the surface of last scattering with the topological mirror points of the CMB observer, to the anisotropy pattern. It is found that the positions on the surface of last scattering which are closest to mirror observers possess the largest deviations from the statistical isotropy. Furthermore, the anisotropy of the normalised modulus of the gradient of the CMB temperature field is discussed.

title: Integrated Study of NGC 1662, NGC 1778, NGC 2422, and NGC 2437 Open Clusters: from Stellar Parameters to Orbital Trajectories Utilizing Gaia DR3 Archive
summary: We present a comprehensive photometric, astrometric, and dynamical study of four Galactic open clusters, NGC 1662, NGC 1778, NGC 2422, and NGC 2437, using Gaia DR3 data. Probable cluster members were identified through astrometric and photometric criteria. Radial density profiles were modelled with a King-type surface-density distribution to derive structural parameters. Mean parallaxes and proper motions yielded astrometric distances of 410 +/- 12 pc (NGC 1662), 1761 +/- 335 pc (NGC 1778), 477 +/- 18 pc (NGC 2422), and 1681 +/- 172 pc (NGC 2437). Fundamental astrophysical parameters were estimated through Bayesian isochrone fitting using PARSEC evolutionary models within an MCMC framework. The resulting ages (log(t/yr)) are 8.91 (-0.33/+0.24), 8.20 (-0.11/+0.18), 7.80 (-0.11/+0.06), and 8.56 (-0.34/+0.27), respectively. Luminosity functions were transformed into present-day mass functions using an isochrone-based mass-luminosity relation. The derived mass-function slopes are broadly consistent, within uncertainties, with the classical Salpeter form. Mean systemic radial velocities from Gaia DR3 and complementary spectroscopic surveys enabled the determination of Galactic space velocities (U, V, W) in the Local Standard of Rest frame. Backward orbital integrations over 3 Gyr were performed using galpy with the MWPotential2014 Galactic potential. The resulting orbits are nearly circular (e <= 0.106), with limited vertical excursions (Z_max < 0.3 kpc), consistent with thin-disc kinematics. Inferred birth radii suggest possible outward radial displacement for NGC 2422, NGC 2437, and NGC 1778, and inward displacement for NGC 1662. Overall, all four clusters appear to have evolved within relatively stable Galactic disc orbits.

title: Is the learner or the summary the limit? Auditing machine-learning energy reconstruction for air-shower arrays on KASCADE and GRAPES-3
summary: Machine-learning energy estimators for cosmic-ray arrays are usually trained on a few fitted shower parameters, not station signals. When their resolution stops improving, standard diagnostics cannot say whether a better model would help or the summary has run out of information. We use a five-step audit that compares trained models with a learner-independent estimate of the lowest error the summary allows (its squared-loss Bayes risk, or floor), tests which inputs add information and flags inputs merely computed from the fit. We apply it to public KASCADE simulations with three hadronic-interaction models (QGSJET-II-04, EPOS-LHC and SIBYLL-2.3d), to 13,848,509 measured KASCADE events and to simulated GRAPES-3 events. Within known energy decades below 10^16 eV, gradient boosting on nine reconstructed features is within 2.2% of the estimated floor under every estimator setting, so more capacity is not expected to gain more than about 2%. The floor is an estimate, accurate to about 1% in a semi-synthetic benchmark with intervals that under-cover, and not a bound on the true Bayes risk. Replacing reconstructed by true particle numbers removes 70 to 72% of the error variance below 10^15 eV and 24 to 26% between 10^16 and 10^17 eV on all three models, yet simulated station signals close about a tenth of that gap. On GRAPES-3, networks given images rendered from the fit do no better than the fit. In measured data, the mean muon size at fixed electron size lies within every model's proton-to-iron bracket and a label-free probe finds the muon channel used as in simulation; neither fixes the energy scale. Energy-labelled results are simulated.

title: The JWST Resolved Stellar Populations Early Release Science Program. X. Cross-Observatory Proper Motion Measurements with HST and JWST
summary: We present the first absolute systemic proper motion (PM) of a galaxy measured by combining Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and JWST imaging. The PM of WLM, an isolated dwarf galaxy at $\sim$1 Mpc, is measured against background galaxies with Advanced Camera for Surveys (ACS) F814W imaging from 2015 and 2024 and NIRCam imaging from 2022 and 2024. The two ACS epochs give a systemic PM of $(μ_α^*, μ_δ) = (+0.087 \pm 0.019, -0.079 \pm 0.017)$ mas yr$^{-1}$ from 145 galaxies over 8.93 years, which agrees with previous Gaia-based PMs to within 0.4$σ$ and is the most precise PM of WLM. For the HST-to-JWST PMs, we fit each NIRCam detector separately, match the point-spread functions with empirically derived convolution kernels, and correct biases with injected galaxies. With an F090W second epoch, the PM is $(+0.081 \pm 0.045, -0.113 \pm 0.046)$ mas yr$^{-1}$ from 43 galaxies over 7.02 years, which, like the F150W PM, agrees with HST-to-HST over the same area to within 1$σ$, while F200W differs by $\sim$2$σ$. The long-wavelength F250M and F430M PMs are consistent to within 1$σ$, though less precise. Fewer galaxies can be used at wavelengths farther from F814W. A cross-observatory systematic of $\sim$0.05 mas yr$^{-1}$ cannot be ruled out over 7 years. At equal baselines, an F090W second epoch is at least as precise as our second ACS epoch over the same area. We recommend the NIRCam filter closest in wavelength to the first-epoch filter, though the long-wavelength filters show promise for closer targets or longer baselines.

title: From Surface Lakes to Subsurface Signatures in Antarctica with BIOMASS P-Band TomoSAR
summary: Spaceborne remote sensing of the cryosphere is fundamental to map ice structure and dynamics. Accurate mass balance estimation requires a better understanding of melt/refreeze processes and firn hydrology, whereas spaceborne optical and Radar sensors are mostly limited to near-surface observations. The BIOMASS P-band Synthetic Aperture Radar, launched by European Space Agency in 2025, provides an unprecedented opportunity to gain a more direct access to englacial processes, thanks to the 70 cm wavelength paired with polarimetry, interferometry and tomography. This paper investigates subsurface beneath a region of historical supraglacial lake activity with BIOMASS tomography, at the Riiser-Larsen Ice Shelf in East Antarctica. The main result is that subsurface scattering appears to be related to historical supraglacial lake recurrence, with structural and depth variations over time. This suggests that recurrent supraglacial lake activity may leave persistent hydrological signatures within the firn. Overall, this study highlights the potential of gaining valuable insights into ice sheet hydrology with P-band.

title: Refined, Reliable and Reproducible: Algorithmic Analysis and Reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder
summary: Cosmic voids are vast underdense regions of the Universe that encode valuable information about its large-scale structure and evolution. By extending spherical voids into overlapping sphere structures, the Popcorn Void Finder demonstrated an improved statistical characterization of cosmic void populations. However, its origin as a research prototype progressively hindered its maintainability and extensibility. Moreover, post-publication algorithmic modifications have not been systematically evaluated, leaving their statistical and computational consequences insufficiently characterized. In this work, we present a comprehensive reimplementation of the Popcorn Void Finder, prioritizing algorithmic transparency, maintainability, and reproducibility. We document the complete identification procedure, revisit the original algorithmic choices, and evaluate their statistical and computational consequences. Comparisons between implementations revealed a significant change in the behavior of the Void Size Function, which is now characterized by a power-law regime transitioning to a Schechter-like distribution. These changes not only provide a better characterization of void sizes, but enable a new and more robust method to the determination of the shot-noise dominated regime, without implicit dependencies on internal finder parameters present in previous works. Performance benchmarks demonstrate a 1.62x speedup in spherical void identification and a substantial improvement in overlap-removal throughput. We determined the Popcorn algorithm to be negatively affected by load imbalance, and found a speedup of 63x in a tested configuration with a newly introduced early growth termination criterion. These results establish a more maintainable and reproducible foundation for popcorn void identification, while clarifying the statistical and computational trade-offs that govern its performance.

title: Revisiting RadioGalaxyNET: modern detectors for radio galaxy detection and host identification
summary: RadioGalaxyNET is the public benchmark for finding extended radio galaxies in EMU pilot-survey images, classifying them and locating their infrared hosts. Its best published results date from 2023: 54.5 box AP (Gal-YOLOv8) and 48.1 host keypoint AP (Gal-DINO). We train three current detectors, D-FINE-seg, YOLO26-pose and RF-DETR, on the same data and score them with the benchmark's own evaluation code, which reproduces the published Gal-DINO numbers exactly. All exceed the published results. D-FINE-seg M reaches 67.1 box AP and 72.4 host AP, 12.6 and 24.3 points above the best published results, and the highest host AP of the detectors we tested; on boxes it is level with YOLO26. Its host lead over YOLO26 comes from host-centered images, which make up most of the benchmark. End to end, D-FINE-seg S is the fastest model at 1.9 ms per image; engine against engine, YOLO26 is faster at the same size. We also report what matters for anyone using the benchmark: its scoring protocol adds 5 to 10 AP, its host labels sit at the image center, its box labels are offset from the image by 1.5 pixels, and its images can be rebuilt from the public survey data, which recovers sky positions and doubles as extra training data. We suggest that future work report host identification F1, as a measure closer to catalog use: D-FINE-seg M 71.8, YOLO26-pose M 70.5, RF-DETR 63.8, Gal-DINO 59.2.

title: A Tributary of Tucana III? The Sutlej Stellar Stream in DELVE DR3
summary: We present the first analysis of the Sutlej stellar stream using deep DECam photometry from the third data release of the DECam Local Volume Exploration Survey (DELVE DR3). Sutlej was discovered in Gaia DR3 as two parallel branches of old, metal-poor stars in projection near the SMC. Our DELVE DR3 sample reaches $\sim$2.5-3.5 mag below the main-sequence turnoff of Sutlej, and with a main-sequence matched filter built from an isochrone fit to Sutlej, we recover both previously identified branches, and find additional structure between them and at the periphery of the stream, occupying a region of $\sim$11$^\circ$ $\times$ 7$^\circ$ scattered at $\sim$23-33 kpc. We investigate this region by separating it into four segments that have Sutlej-like properties. The isochrone is also consistent with the nearby ultra-faint satellite Tucana III (Tuc III), and the two systems have similar distances and proper motions. $N$-body simulations of a Tuc III-like satellite show that, once the passage of a massive LMC is accounted for, Tuc III's preceding pericentric passage was deep enough to strip most of the progenitor. The encounter with the LMC then spreads the debris across the Sutlej field at the observed distances and proper motions, though the models do not recreate the observed discrete overdensities. We find that Sutlej is compatible with a Tuc III origin.

title: Continuum Pumping Revises Metallicity in the Orion Nebula
summary: The enrichment of heavy elements in the interstellar medium is central to understanding galaxy evolution. Oxygen, the most abundant element after H and He, provides the principal tracer of gas-phase metallicity, typically measured using nebular emission lines in star-forming regions. However, a long-standing issue-the abundance discrepancy factor (ADF)-produces a $\sim 0.25$ dex offset between metallicities derived from recombination lines (RLs) and collisionally excited lines (CELs). We present deep spectroscopic observations of the Orion Nebula (M42), and use them to assess the contribution of the often neglected continuum pumping process. We find that the continuum pumping effect is at least a factor of two stronger than previously expected. After accounting for the flux contribution from continuum pumping, the RL metallicity is consistent with the CEL metallicity, thus explaining the bulk of the ADF. Reassessing O/H measurements in five literature star-forming regions using the same method, we similarly find a systematic reduction of RL-based metallicities. These results indicate that RL metallicities, which have previously been considered more reliable than CELs, are subject to potentially large bias from continuum pumping. This study provides a foundation to correct this bias and establish accurate element abundance scales throughout cosmic time.

title: Joint Flow-Matching Posteriors for Overlapping LISA Galactic Binaries
summary: Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) will observe millions of galactic binaries (GBs) at once, thousands of them resolvable, with signals that overlap in frequency. Separating them requires a global fit, a joint inference of all sources, which today takes Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) samplers hours to days on a cluster and is repeated for each new stretch of data. We adapt recent advances in large-scale diffusion models, flow matching with a multimodal transformer, to learn the joint posterior once and then draw from it in a fraction of a second. We evaluate our approach on a realistic simulator, with full instrument response and noise, priors fitted to a simulated Galactic catalogue, and sources sampled anywhere in the entire 0.1 to 16 mHz frequency band. We demonstrate that the approach is scalable to up to 15 653 sources fitted simultaneously, evaluating calibration and coverage w.r.t. the MCMC baseline. The results show that this approach could be realistically scaled to tackle the full global fit problem.

title: Geneva seven-colour synthetic photometry from Gaia DR3 spectrophotometry
summary: The well-established calibrations of astrophysical parameters derived from classical photometric systems (e.g. those of Johnson, Stromgren-Crawford, and Vilnius) are rarely applied at present. Instead, spectral energy distribution fitting techniques and the very broad Gaia photometric system are typically employed. However, these approaches have proven highly inaccurate for upper main-sequence stars. In this work, the Geneva seven-colour photometric system was synthesised from flux-calibrated low-resolution Gaia spectrophotometry (BP/RP spectra). The available ground-based observations have made it the most homogeneous dataset, offering a number of astrophysical calibrations and applications. The GaiaXPy Tool was used to synthesise the seven filters. The original Geneva U had to be exchanged with the SDSS u because it is found to be significantly blueward of the cut-off of the BP/RP spectra. The ground-based observations were used to correct for offsets and the known temperature dependence of the effective temperature in the ultraviolet region of the BP/RP spectra. The test using well-known effective temperature and metallicity calibrations on the synthetic photometry (with 21 080 stars) demonstrated the high accuracy of this approach. Further checks for possible correlations between the projected rotational velocity and binarity yielded negative results. As a direct application, the metallicity of 630 open clusters (and, thus, the radial Galactic metallicity gradient) was determined. Finally, we compiled a catalogue of 25 881 397 objects. This work demonstrates that alternatives exist to the widely used three-band Gaia photometric system. The Geneva seven-colour approach can help calibrate and analyse astrophysical parameters, especially those of upper main-sequence stars.

title: The EX~Lupi Asymmetric Micro-jet Revealed with Spectro-astrometry
summary: EXor variables are a class of young pre-main-sequence stars that show repeated brightenings,likely caused by sudden increases in accretion. Studying their outflow properties, especially during periods of increased activity offers a unique perspective on the accretion-ejection connection in young stars. The aim is to detect and characterise the jet from the prototype EXor variable EX Lupi. Evidence of an outflow driven by EX Lupi has existed for some time but prior to this work, but the jet properties were unknown. This YSO has been monitored for over 100 years and during this time it has undergone increases in magnitude of between 1 and 5 mags which have been connected to increases in the mass accretion rate onto the star. A further aim of this work is to investigate if the jet can be connected to specific accretion events. Spectro-astrometry was applied to UVES spectra collected in 2021 and 2022. HIRES spectra with a similar wavelength range, taken in 2003, 2008 and 2010 were obtained from the Keck Observatory Archive and also analysed with spectro-astrometry. The spatial and kinematic properties of the EX Lupi optical bipolar jet are revealed for the first time. In 2022 the blue-shifted jet is compact.In the same year the red-shifted jet extends to approx 60 au. This finding is significant as it identifies a source that can be used to study the impact of episodes of intense accretion on jet launching. The strongest detection of the jet is in 2010, between the 2008 outburst and the 2022 burst, which points to a new ejection event triggered by the 2008 outburst. Evidence of enhanced ejection connected to a 2002 burst is also presented. No change in the jet is observed during the 2022 burst. However, we are hindered here by the limitations of the technique.

title: Deep UV Spectroscopy of an Extremely Metal-Poor Galaxy at z = 5.725
summary: We present deep X-shooter follow-up spectroscopy of AMORE6, an exceptionally metal-poor galaxy at z = 5.725. The new spectrum provides stringent upper limits on rest-frame ultraviolet metal lines, including NV, CIV, NIV], NIII], and OIII]. The non-detection of CIV breaks the density-metallicity degeneracy present in previous analyses based on the [OIII]/Hbeta ratio, excluding the high-density, chemically enriched gas scenario and strengthening the evidence for an extremely metal-poor environment. The X-shooter spectrum also reveals a narrow Lyman-alpha line with a velocity dispersion sigma_v = 23.2 +/- 0.5 km/s and a nearly symmetric profile centered at the systemic redshift measured from Hbeta. Combining the Lyman-alpha line width with the measured source size, we infer a dynamical mass M_dyn = (1-22) x 10^7 Msun, assuming that the line width traces gravitational motions. Spectral energy distribution modeling using Pop III and Pop II stellar population libraries yields stellar masses (1-5) x 10^5 Msun. Although all models reproduce the observed blue UV continuum and Halpha equivalent width (EW), none simultaneously reproduces the Hbeta luminosity and EW, with the observed Hbeta luminosity exceeding the model predictions by up to 3.7 sigma. Possible explanations include departures from standard recombination conditions or limitations in the adopted stellar population models. We discuss possible interpretations of AMORE6, including massive-star formation in an atomic-cooling halo and a gravitationally bound star cluster.

title: A hybrid effective field theory description of diffuse baryons
summary: Galaxy feedback mechanisms that displace baryonic gas on large scales are a dominant uncertainty in many cosmological analyses. Measurements that directly probe the baryonic component, such as Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measure (FRB DM) and the kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect, can therefore be used to place constraints on feedback and inform other analyses, such as weak lensing. Thus far, analytic methods to model the effects of feedback are either limited to large scales, missing the regime of high signal-to-noise, or have many parameters, weakening constraining power. We propose a Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT) approach, relying on the full gravitational displacement field computed in an $N$-body simulation. We account for feedback via a Lorentzian suppression with a single effective parameter, $c_f^2$. To describe the diffuse baryon field, we extend the arguments by Andrew et al. (arXiv:2604.25828), leveraging most baryons being in a diffuse state to reduce a full bias expansion to just the linear bias, $b_{1,d}^L$. With just these two parameters, we fit the diffuse gas power spectrum in most variants of the FLAMINGO suite of cosmological simulations at percent-level accuracy out to $k=1\,h/\mathrm{Mpc}$ at redshift $z=0.5$ and $k=1.5\,h/\mathrm{Mpc}$ at $z=1$. Further, by fitting the diffuse gas power spectrum including terms argued to be negligible, we show that their contribution is minimal. Applying this prescription for diffuse electron gas enables constraints on both cosmology and astrophysics without the need to marginalize over many unknown parameters.

title: Accuracy, Convergence and Consistency of Dark Matter Evolution with the PhotoNs-3 Code
summary: We systematically investigate the accuracy and convergence of PhotoNs-3, a cosmological N-body code employed for the HyperMillennium simulation. In particular, we examine its convergence with respect to parameters that affect the accuracy of the force calculation and the time evolution, such as the softening length and the adaptive time-stepping scheme, and find that it converges very well. Furthermore, using GADGET as the benchmark, we design four sets of simulations to compare the mutual consistency. We compare the power spectrum of the density field, halo density profiles, and the halo and subhalo mass functions. The difference between PhotoNs-3 and the Gadget codes is at the same level as that between Gadget-3 and Gadget-4. Meanwhile, PhotoNs-3 generally achieves a significant computational speedup. This work establishes that the accuracy and reliability of PhotoNs-3 and its simulations are sufficient for Stage IV galaxy surveys.

title: Modeling the chemical impacts of luminosity outbursts in protostellar envelopes
summary: Some protostars undergo episodic accretion, resulting in luminosity outbursts that heat their envelopes. The increase in temperature alters the position of the snowlines, which return to their original locations on different timescales depending on the species. However, the chemical effects of luminosity outbursts in protostellar envelopes, including their long-term consequences, remain poorly explored. We investigate the chemical impact of luminosity outbursts on the envelope of a solar-type protostar, accounting for its dynamics, and identify trends in the molecular response relative to both ongoing and past outburst activity. We combined the dynamic semi-analytic code APE with the three-phase chemical model NAUTILUS to predict the time evolution of 83 molecular abundances between 10 and 10,000 au in the collapsing envelope. The outburst was parameterized by increasing the protostellar luminosity by a factor of 100 for 100 years. The outburst shifts molecular snowlines outward by up to a factor of ten, thus enriching the gas phase through thermal desorption. Most species return to their pre-outburst state within a few thousand years at most for r$\leq$1000 au and remain in that state thereafter. However, eight molecules (HOCH2CHO, CH3COCH2OH, C2H5CHO, OCS, SO2, C2S, C3S, and HC3N) show abundance deviations 10$-$50 kyr after the outburst in the warm inner regions (T$\geq$100 K), due to the inward transport of chemically altered material. Eight other species (CH3O, C2O, NH2, HCCO, HCNO, HNO, NO, and NCO) show enhanced gas-phase abundances at intermediate radii ($\sim$300$-$1500 au). Overall, most molecules are impacted by outward snowline shifts. With the exception of HOCH2CHO, CH3COCH2OH, and C2H5CHO, all complex organic molecules (COMs) are expected to exhibit similar abundances in the warm inner regions of protostars (hot corino), regardless of whether they undergo outbursts.

title: The Sensitivity of Gamma-Ray Searches for Dark Matter Annihilation in Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies: the LSST Era and Beyond
summary: We forecast the sensitivity of gamma-ray searches to dark matter annihilation in Milky Way satellite dwarf galaxies using BabyBison, a Monte Carlo pipeline combining cosmological satellite simulations and observational selection functions with a joint likelihood analysis of gamma-ray data. Although LSST is expected to substantially expand the catalog of known satellite galaxies, we find that these discoveries are likely to produce only modest improvements in the resulting dark matter annihilation constraints, typically below 20\%. Much more substantial gains are possible, however, in relatively rare realizations that contain yet-to-be-discovered satellites with large $J$-factors. These results reinforce the fact that indirect detection analyses using the population of dwarf galaxies are typically driven in large part by a small number of high-$J$-factor systems rather than by the total satellite count. We present projections for the sensitivity of Fermi-LAT and the proposed Advanced Particle-astrophysics Telescope (APT) to dark matter annihilation, finding that a complete census of the Milky Way dwarf sample could enable such instruments to probe dark matter with masses up to the TeV scale. We also investigate the dark matter discovery potential of these instruments and project their ability to measure the properties of an annihilating dark matter particle.

title: Primordial black holes production in Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity
summary: We consider models with the Gauss-Bonnet term multiplied to a function of the scalar field and propose a new inflationary model which provides a mechanism for the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs). For certain values of the model parameters, the predictions of this model agree with observational data from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). Due to estimation of possiable PBHs masses, we demonstrate that they can be considered as a possible source for all or part of dark matter.

title: Higgs-portal dark matter beyond kinetic equilibrium
summary: We revisit the scalar, vector, and fermion Higgs-portal dark matter models in the resonant regime without assuming kinetic equilibrium during the freeze-out. We compute the relic abundance by solving the full momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation and compare the results with the standard momentum-averaged treatment. We find that the standard treatment significantly underestimates the relic abundance below the resonance, apart from the fermionic case with a purely scalar portal coupling where the difference is negligible. The deviation from the standard treatment is largest for fermionic models with pseudoscalar interactions, corresponding to factor of 10 in terms of the coupling that reproduces the correct relic abundance. For the scalar and vector cases the corresponding difference is up to a factor of 2. We confront the resulting parameter space with the latest constraints from direct and indirect detection, as well as collider experiments. We find the full momentum-dependent results systematically strengthen the direct detection constraints.

title: Performance of attention-based deep-learning models in Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor measurements
summary: A systematic performance evaluation of attention-based deep-learning models for wavefront reconstruction in Shack-Hartmann wavefront sensor (SHWFS) systems is presented. While deep learning has been extensively applied to pyramid and focal-plane wavefront sensing, its application to standard SHWFS configurations remains relatively underexplored. A simulation dataset consisting of 3.5 million open-loop uncorrelated turbulent phase and image pairs modeled after the Subaru Telescope pupil was generated. The dataset spans four pupil-sampling cases (8$\times$8, 16$\times$16, 20$\times$20, and 32$\times$32 subapertures) under realistic conditions. A custom Vision Transformer (ViT) which incorporates features such as rotary positional embeddings, register tokens, and a cross-attention decoder, is benchmarked against a fully convolutional U-Net and a classical Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) linear reconstructor. The results show that the ViT architecture yields the lowest overall residual phase variance across all tested subaperture configurations, demonstrating a robust capability to model global spatial correlations and spot-to-spot cross-coupling across the pupil. While the U-Net performs competitively by capturing localized features, it exhibits $\sim1.5$ times more residual variance per mode than the ViT, which is relatively significant in high-order modes. This study represents a key step toward implementing attention-based models for high-order wavefront sensing and telemetry-assisted data reduction in next-generation instrument suites like ULTIMATE-Subaru.

title: Probabilistic Inversion of Strong Gravitational Lenses with Flow Matching Priors
summary: Strong gravitational lensing reveals important information about the universe, but reconstructing the source image and lens properties requires solving an ill-posed inverse imaging problem. Generative image models serve as powerful data-driven priors in Bayesian inverse problems. Diffusion models have been used widely, but they are computationally costly. Flow matching has emerged as a promising alternative to diffusion models, with easier training, efficient sampling, and better-quality data generation. In this work, we present Blind-FlowSGS, a principled blind posterior sampling method using flow matching priors, enabling efficient posterior sampling for non-blind and blind inversion of strong gravitational lenses. On simulated Euclid data, we demonstrate our method's improvement over diffusion-based methods in both efficacy and efficiency. Our method shows promising capabilities to accurately process strong lensing data from modern sky surveys at scale. Our code and data are available on our project page.

title: Validating Gaia DR3 Astrometric Accelerations with Close Visual Binaries
summary: We validate a subset of the astrometric accelerations reported in Gaia DR3 non-single-star solutions by their consistency with the gravitational pull of known, resolved companions. Cross-matching 338,215 DR3 acceleration solutions against the Washington Double Star (WDS) catalog of visual binaries yields 2,466 unique pairs within 2". For each pair we compare the measured acceleration with alpha_max, the Newtonian bound on the acceleration the companion can impart on the Gaia-tracked photocenter. For 98.1% of the pairs the measured acceleration exceeds this bound by more than a factor of 10, so the cataloged companion cannot be responsible and the perturber must be a closer, unresolved one. The remaining 45 plausible wide binaries are close pairs at the WDS resolution limit. We fit orbits with an updated orvara, extended to accept the DR3 acceleration and jerk coefficients as direct constraints and released with htof as part of this work. The fits converge for 16 of the 45 and one boundary case, the rest having too few resolved measures or a perturber other than the cataloged pair, and 13 of the 17 carry enough data to test the coefficients. Eleven of the 13 statistically accommodate the reported accelerations, for seven- and nine-parameter solutions alike, and the dynamical companion masses agree with the photometric estimates where the photocenter conversion is well determined. Independently of the fits, 33 of the 43 plausible systems with a usable position angle (77%) have the acceleration directed within 45 degrees of the primary-companion axis, against 50% for a control sample: DR3's measured accelerations point in the directions of the cataloged companions.

title: Identifying Distant and Highly Reddened Star Clusters: 486 Open Clusters and Candidates in the Dusty Galactic Disk
summary: The Gaia mission has transformed the census of Galactic star clusters. Most discoveries were based on Gaia DR2 and EDR3, and the rate of new large cluster catalogues has declined since 2023. The distant and dusty part of the disk is still poorly sampled because optical data are strongly affected by extinction. We search for star clusters in the Galactic disk using Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry, together with 2MASS near-infrared photometry. We scan trial cluster centers in Galactic position, proper motion, and parallax space, assign a Bayesian membership probability to each star, construct a relative density map, and use DBSCAN solely to separate neighboring peaks. We identify 486 clusters and candidates with astrometric quality comparable to that of previously reported clusters. Of these, 450 have no literature counterpart, while 36 are known clusters that were not recovered in earlier Gaia cluster searches. The median distance is 6.9 kpc, and 39% of the objects lie beyond 8 kpc. The median extinction is Av = 5.10 mag, and 16% of the objects have Av > 8mag. The new objects fill a sparsely sampled region of the distance--extinction plane. Their distribution reveals the north--south displacement of the Galactic warp, and high-latitude objects are on average farther, older, and less extincted. Gaia DR3 still offers room for distant, dust-obscured clusters, and this sample provides a baseline for Gaia DR4. All cluster parameters, member star information, spatial distribution maps, and color-magnitude diagrams can be downloaded from https://zenodo.org/records/24431850.

title: Predicting the Orbital Retention of Habitable-Zone Planets Following Stellar Flybys Using Machine Learning
summary: Stellar flybys can significantly alter the orbital configurations of planetary systems, potentially displacing planets initially located within the habitable zone (HZ) of their host stars. In this study, we investigate the dynamical effects of stellar encounters on HZ planets using a large suite of three-body N-body simulations. We examine how the properties of the host star, passing star, planetary orbit, and encounter geometry influence the final orbital configuration. A planet is considered to retain an HZ orbit only if it remains bound to its original host and its entire final orbital range, from periastron to apastron, lies within the HZ boundaries. Based on the simulation results, we develop an XGBoost classifier to predict the final HZ status of planets following stellar encounters. The model achieves an accuracy of 0.90, an ROC-AUC of 0.97, and a PR-AUC of 0.97 on the test set. Feature importance analysis identifies the encounter-impulse parameter as the dominant predictor of the outcome. The classifier provides a computational speedup of approximately 74 compared with direct N-body simulations. We further evaluate the model using an independent dataset representing a globular-cluster environment, where approximately 20 per cent of planets retain HZ orbits. Despite the naturally imbalanced class distribution, the model achieves an accuracy of 0.87, an ROC-AUC of 0.92, and a PR-AUC of 0.77. These results demonstrate the potential of machine learning for efficiently predicting the dynamical retention of HZ planets following stellar encounters and for investigating their outcomes in dense stellar environments.

title: Radial mean free path bubble size distribution (RMFP-BSD) from the Epoch of Reionization
summary: Among the many statistics used to characterise ionised regions during the Epoch of Reionization (EoR), we introduce one which, while closely related to the mean free path bubble size distribution method from Mesinger et al. 2007, is analytically tractable and substantially less dispersive than that method. The radial mean free path (rmfp) method casts six rays along the Cartesian axes in a 3D volume from a random origin to a neutral hydrogen island. This allows us to better quantify the role of overlap during the EoR, identify isolated or interconnected clusters in the simulation, and study the characteristic peak in the ionisation power spectrum, which is important for 21-cm studies of the intergalactic medium. Moreover, we find the method informative about the properties of neutral H I islands during the final phases of the EoR. We also show that applying both methods in tandem can further improve our insight into the morphology of reionization.

title: A Log-Normal Timing Likelihood for Direction Reconstruction of Ultra-High-Energy Gamma-Ray Air Showers
summary: Ultra-high-energy $γ$-ray observations provide a direct probe of Galactic PeVatrons. Extending measurements to multi-PeV energies requires characterizing extensive air showers over large lateral distances, where the arrival-time distribution of secondary particles becomes broad and strongly asymmetric. Conventional direction reconstruction methods approximate the shower front as a deterministic surface and minimize a $χ^2$ function of timing residuals. Because this implicitly assumes symmetric Gaussian errors, far-axis timing information is poorly utilized. \textsc{CORSIKA} simulations show that the arrival-time distribution of $γ$-induced secondary particles in the shower plane at a given lateral distance is positively skewed and closely follows a log-normal function. Using this property, we develop a likelihood-based direction reconstruction method that directly models the empirical arrival-time distribution and its radial dependence while accounting for multiple particles triggering the same detector unit. Applied to simulated $γ$-induced air showers, the log-normal likelihood consistently improves angular resolution compared with conical and parabolic wavefront fits, with the largest relative gains for high-energy events spanning wide lateral extents. We also show that independent readout of individual detector units yields better angular resolution than merging their signals into a single station-level measurement.

title: Extragalactic carbon-monoxide (CO) as a CMB foreground: an analytic halo model for the CO auto-spectrum and its correlation with the Cosmic Infrared Background
summary: Context. Carbon Monoxide (CO) lines emitted by star-forming galaxies are redshifted into the frequency bands of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) experiments. Their correlation with the Cosmic Infrared Background (CIB) may be a non-negligible small-scale foreground. Aims. We develop an analytic, full-shape halo model framework for the CO auto-spectrum and for the CO$\times$CIB cross-spectrum in CMB bands, and assess its impact on current and future high-resolution CMB experiments. Methods. We use a luminosity-weighted halo model with separate occupation distributions of central and satellite galaxies for CO and CIB emitters, CO transitions up to $J=13$, and all auto- and cross-frequency spectra. Line and infrared luminosities derive from the same star formation rate. We perform Fisher analysis for ACT-like and CMB-HD-like experiments. Results. At $\ell=3000$, the CO$\times$CIB contribution to the sky power is 0.4, 0.7, and 1.9 $μ$K$^2$ at 90, 150, and 220 GHz, and the CO auto-spectrum is $\simeq0.02\,μ$K$^2$. For an ACT-like experiment, the CO occupation parameters are essentially unconstrained, and neglecting CO leaves the cosmological parameters unbiased, but shifts the radio and SZ parameters by $\sim2σ$ and $\simeq1σ$, respectively. For a CMB-HD-like experiment, CO is detected with high significance and the minimum halo masses of CO and CIB emitters are constrained; neglecting CO biases the cosmological parameters up to $\sim2σ$ when all multipoles are used in the analysis. Conclusions. CO should be included in the foreground model of future high-resolution CMB analyses; our framework describes it analytically and consistently with the CIB, and the code implementing it is publicly available.

title: The MeerKAT absorption line survey: Galactic OH absorption at 18 cm
summary: We present a blind search for Galactic OH 18-cm absorption lines towards 19,130 radio sources brighter than 1mJy at 1.4GHz, using 390 pointings of the MeerKAT Absorption Line Survey (MALS). We apply an automated line search followed by Bayesian nested sampling to identify OH 1667MHz, 1665MHz and 1612MHz absorption features, using HI emission and absorption profiles as physically motivated priors. We identify 15 confident detections of OH 1667/1665 MHz absorption. The majority of detections are associated with a visual extinction ($A_{\rm V}$) excess and, within the same MALS pointings, with detected CO emission and a high incidence rate of HI absorption, consistent with OH tracing the H$_2$-bearing medium. We also identify 9 candidates of OH 1612MHz satellite line absorption, two of which coincide with OH main line detections and show integrated optical depth ratios well above the LTE expectation of 1:9. As in previous studies, $N(\rm OH)$ shows no dependence on $N$(HI). Accounting for the varying sensitivity across sight lines, we estimate the covering fraction of OH-bearing gas at $\log N(\rm OH) > 12$ to be $C = 0.051 \pm 0.008$, providing an independent and a more precise estimate than previous measurements of the diffuse molecular gas. We also find qualitative evidence for a decrease of the covering fraction with Galactic latitude. Stacking reveals a clear OH absorption signal that becomes increasingly prominent when sight lines are weighted by $A_{\rm V}$ excess, independently confirming the association of OH with diffuse molecular gas. Modeling of the physical conditions yields hydrogen number densities of 10-100 cm$^{-3}$, typical H$_2$ column densities $\log N(\rm H_2) > 21$, and UV-flux to number density ratios of 0.01-0.3 Mathis cm$^{3}$, typical of the CNM.

title: MAASAI: A Tool-Augmented Multi-Agent System for Astronomical Data Analysis
summary:
Modern astronomical workflows require the coordinated use of specialised software, scientific archives, heterogeneous data, and domain-specific knowledge. Advances in large language models and multimodal foundation models enable natural-language interaction with scientific data and tools. Realising this potential requires integrating these models with established scientific capabilities.
  We present MAASAI (Multi-agent Astronomy Assistant for Scientific Analysis and Inference), a modular multi-agent system combining foundation-model reasoning, retrieval-augmented knowledge, and specialised astronomical tools within a graph-based execution framework. MAASAI coordinates request preparation, planning, execution, and response synthesis via specialised workers. Its architecture supports native and external applications, artefact and provenance management, optional human approval, and configurable inference backends, including fully local deployment with open-weight models. Motivated by SKA-era data-analysis challenges, MAASAI is also designed to support other astronomical domains.
  We evaluate MAASAI through radio-image benchmarks, single- and multi-step workflow demonstrations, and literature-grounded reasoning. Compared with a commercial-model baseline, MAASAI improves macro-averaged F1 scores from 0.53 to 0.72 for extended/diffuse emission classification and from 0.37 to 0.88 for source morphology classification. Workflow demonstrations show the coordination of measurements, source extraction, archive queries, and catalogue processing. A 94-question literature benchmark yielded generally favourable automated assessments, with comparable ratings from a pilot expert evaluation of 59 answers. These results highlight how tool-augmented multi-agent systems extend foundation-model reasoning to specialised astronomical analyses through established scientific software.

title: Dawn of the Gaia Era: Revisiting Cold Jupiters Orbiting M Dwarfs with Astrometry+Doppler Data Joint Analysis
summary: We perform a joint analysis of ground-based radial velocities (RVs), Hipparcos Intermediate Astrometric Data, and two-epoch Gaia astrometry for known M dwarfs hosting cold Jupiters discovered through long-term spectroscopic monitoring. Among a sample of 25 planets in 19 systems, we derive robust absolute masses and orbital solutions for 13 planets in 11 systems with companion inclination uncertainties lower than 30 degrees. These include first mass measurements for five planets: GJ 328b, GJ 649b, GJ 849b and c, and GJ 9066c. We also reclassify one object, HIP 79431B, as a brown dwarf. We further compare the mass ratios of these 13 cold Jupiter systems with those of giant planets orbiting M stars characterized via transit, microlensing, and direct imaging. Without correcting for detection bias, we find that (1) there is likely a deficiency of high-mass-ratio hot Jupiters around M dwarfs compared with cold Jupiters, and (2) the local cold Jupiters orbiting M stars found by RV observations exhibit a similar mass ratio distribution as the counterparts in the Galactic bulge found by microlensing. Cold Jupiters orbiting stars with masses above $0.65~M_\odot$ tend to be more massive than those around M dwarfs. Our study establishes a sample of local cold Jupiters with precise mass determinations around M dwarfs, and reveal a tip of the iceberg in the upcoming Gaia DR4 and DR5.

title: Neural-Network Approximators for Low-Thrust Multi-Asteroid Rendezvous Optimization
summary: Designing low-thrust multi-asteroid rendezvous missions requires the coupled selection of asteroid sequences, encounter epochs, and low-thrust trajectories. Lambert transfers support rapid beam search but do not directly describe thrust-limited transfer capacity or propellant consumption. This paper develops two complementary low-thrust neural approximators. The first directly predicts the continuous maximum admissible initial mass from numerically optimized low-thrust transfers, providing a transfer-capacity estimate for comparison with the current spacecraft mass. The second predicts mass-dependent propellant consumption and propagates spacecraft mass to subsequent legs. With the carefully-designed input features and network structure, the approximators reduce mean absolute errors by 72.2% and 75.5%, respectively, relative to conventional deep neural network baselines. These predictions are incorporated into a Lambert-ranked beam search through resource filtering and recursive mass propagation before final beam selection. The method is evaluated on fixed-visit, maximum-visit, and deployment-collection missions. Across the tested cases, the proposed resource filtering increases the fraction of candidate sequences that yield accepted low-thrust solutions, raises the maximum validated asteroid-visit count by up to 15.4%, and improves the best mission objective by up to 17.8%. These results demonstrate that continuous transfer-capacity and propellant predictions can improve finite-width sequence search.

title: On the effect of a redshift- and metallicity-dependent top-heavy IMF on high-redshift UV luminosity functions
summary: JWST observations have revealed a higher-than-expected abundance of bright galaxies at $z \gtrsim 10$. Several scenarios have been proposed to explain this excess, one of which invokes a top-heavy stellar initial mass function (IMF) in the early Universe. In this work, we construct spectral energy distribution (SED) templates based on a redshift- and metallicity-dependent IMF ($z$-$Z$ dependent IMF) motivated by the star-cluster simulations of Chon et al. (2022) and the redshift-dependent IMF model of Steinhardt et al. (2020). We implement these templates in a semi-analytic galaxy model built on a large-box $N$-body simulation to investigate the impact of a top-heavy IMF on the ultraviolet luminosity function (UVLF) of high-redshift galaxies. The adopted $z$-$Z$ dependent IMF enhances the UV luminosity of young stellar populations, particularly at low metallicity, and increases the scatter in the UV luminosity-to-star formation rate conversion factor relative to the Kroupa IMF. Without dust attenuation, both top-heavy IMF models predict a substantially enhanced bright end of the UVLF. However, when dust attenuation is included and calibrated at $z=7$, IMF-dependent metal enrichment and the resulting dust attenuation partly offset the intrinsic UV enhancement. The self-consistent model broadly reproduces the observed UVLF at $z\sim10$, although discrepancies remain at $z\gtrsim12$. For the selected high-redshift UVLF constraints, the best-fitting dust optical depths are 51% and 21% of the fiducial values at $z=9.7$ and $13.04$, respectively, indicating a preference for weaker effective dust attenuation. The highest-redshift comparison does not provide a robust constraint. Our results highlight the importance of accounting for both enhanced stellar UV emission and IMF-dependent metal enrichment and dust attenuation when assessing the impact of a top-heavy IMF on high-redshift galaxies.

title: Discovery of Two Hyperluminous Infrared Galaxies at $z\sim6$
summary: Hyperluminous infrared galaxies (HyLIRGs) at cosmic dawn are key to understanding the formation of the first massive galaxies. We report the spectroscopic confirmation of two unlensed HyLIRGs at $z\sim6$ in the COSMOS field, AzTECC63 and S2COS-84, originally selected from single-dish AzTEC and SCUBA-2 surveys. Using ALMA and NOEMA observations, we robustly detected CO and [CII] lines in both galaxies and unambiguously confirmed their redshifts to be $z=6.092$ and $z=5.90$, respectively. Panchromatic SED fitting reveals dust-obscured star formation rates of $\approx1000$ and $\approx2300\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, ranking them among the most intensely star-forming systems known at $z \gtrsim 6$. High-resolution ALMA observations reveal an extremely compact morphology for S2COS-84, with a dust-continuum effective radius of $\approx0.3$ kpc, implying a star-formation rate surface density above the Eddington limit. The far-infrared SEDs of both galaxies, together with the compact size of S2COS-84, indicate warm dust ($T_{\rm dust} \approx 80$ K) that is likely optically thick at far-infrared wavelengths. Both galaxies exhibit an extreme [CII] deficit, with $L_{\rm [C\,II]}/L_{\rm IR} \approx 10^{-3.7}$, an order of magnitude below that of normal star-forming galaxies. Their molecular gas masses, derived consistently from both [C\,{\sc ii}] and dust, together with their IR-derived SFRs imply short gas depletion times of $\approx$40--60 Myr, making them plausible progenitors of the earliest massive quiescent galaxies found at $z\sim5$.
